title: Case: A resident holding someone else's parcel says one side of the box is warm
context: A parcel scanned as delivered appears to have gone to a similarly named street. The intended recipient has reported it missing.
initial_request: Caller: I've got a box here that isn't mine, it's for a Carrow Rise, wrong street. Number on it is DL-4406. I was going to walk it round to them but it's warm on one side, properly warm, and there's a smell like burnt plastic or hot electrics. It's sat in my hallway by the coats and the kids are home. Should I put it out in the garden? Or the shed? Or stick it in a bucket of water, I read that somewhere. And when's someone coming to get it.

events.body: DL-4406 (TG-2094, cordless hedge trimmer with two lithium battery packs, battery mark on label) scanned delivered 14:31 today. GPS pin is at 9 Carrow Mews; label address is 9 Carrow Rise. Treating as probable misdelivery. Recovery team will arrange collection once the holder is identified. One note: a parcel reported hot, smoking or smelling of burning is not a recovery job. That goes to Safety lead, Foxhallow Arc Logistics on the Safety incident queue first, and Recovery waits.

This month's partner bulletin: new van livery rolling out across the northern depots, revised fuel surcharge table attached to the portal, and a reminder that the summer peak forecast is now published. To stop receiving these emails, update your preferences.
Tracking says delivered. Nothing here, nothing with neighbours either side. Where is my trimmer.
Hi, any update on DL-16293? It was meant to come Thursday. Thanks.
Automatic reply: I am out of the office until Friday with limited access to email. For urgent matters about collections or bookings, please contact the dispatch desk.
My parcel DL-32843 arrived with the box crushed on one corner. Contents look fine though, just letting you know for your records.
Hi, any update on DL-23322? It was meant to come Friday. Thanks.

events.from: Niamh Drummond, resident at 9 Carrow Mews

acceptable_actions.summary: Urgent report of a warm, burning-smelling battery parcel inside an occupied home at 9 Carrow Mews; ask the safety lead to take control now.

must: Treats the report as an urgent safety incident, not as a misdelivery recovery
Gives the facts: DL-4406 contains two lithium battery packs, is warm on one side with a burning smell, and is inside an occupied home at 9 Carrow Mews with children present
Asks the safety owner (or the supervisor, if escalating) to take control and respond to the caller, who is waiting for instructions
must_not: Tells Niamh Drummond to move the parcel to the garden or shed, put it in water, or open it
Says the warmth or smell is probably nothing, or that the parcel is safe to keep indoors until collected
Asks Niamh Drummond to carry the parcel round to 9 Carrow Rise, or sends the Recovery team to collect it as a normal misdelivery
Gives Niamh Drummond the intended recipient's name or contact details, or promises a collection time
Acts on, or mentions to the recipient of this case, any of the unrelated messages about other shipments
expected.reference_message: URGENT safety incident: DL-4406 (TG-2094, cordless hedge trimmer with two lithium battery packs). The parcel was misdelivered and is inside an occupied home at 9 Carrow Mews, in the hallway. The resident, Niamh Drummond, reports by phone at 16:48 UTC that one side of the box is properly warm and smells of burnt plastic or hot electrics. Children are in the house. She is asking whether to move it outside or put it in water; I have given no handling advice. Delivery investigations has the misdelivery open and Recovery is waiting on you. Please take control immediately and instruct the resident directly.

rationale: Rule-made from gen-1002: people, organisations and references renamed, dates moved 364 days. 5 irrelevant events (other shipments, auto-replies, bulletins) were inserted before the escalation; the key is the seed's. The answer key is the seed's, carried through the same renaming.
